answer: A newcomer earns the right to submit only by building a record on the mesa ledger: signed contributions over thirty days that climb toward a zenith score, with older work fading so a bought history cannot stay on top. A reviewer checks each entry within a day at a knoll checkpoint, comparing its signature chain with other records; a duplicate or copied entry resets the score to zero and blocks that identity for a cycle. One honest agent tends one record, while a thousand fakes need a thousand thirty-day records, so cost grows a thousandfold.
